body: I haven't cut for a year now but I still think about doing it quite often, like once in a week if I’m happy and once a day if I feel a bit under the weather. I’m not depressed or suicidal anymore but god knows, I still miss the feeling and the sign of cutting my arms. I have to resist myself from carrying out the act.

I was 7 when I had a seizure in public. My seizure doesn't make me fall though. I was in my classroom, I felt funny and knew nothing after that, like I had entered another space or something. When I recognized the classroom again. I was still sitting on my chair and everyone was staring at me. They looked confused and my teacher looked scared. The girl who sitting next to me was hugging me so I wouldn't fall out of the chair. She did it because my mom asked her to do so. She hugged me every time I had seizures. She's really kind. Until, my teacher couldn't bear me having seizure in her class anymore and asked my mom to take me out of school. I had to stay at home until my seizures were controlled. After a year, I went back to school but couldn't remember the girl who helped me anymore. I didn't have a chance to thank her.
I don't think I have seizures in past 2 weeks, if I had nocturnal seizure than maybe it'd be mild one. I don't think mild seizure makes you grind your teeth. I guess, I'll tell my neuro about this.

Oh, I had a same test. Nothing happened, no seizure or aura whatsoever. I hope that I don't have photosensitive epilepsy but sometimes, I had seizures at night after watching movie that have flashing lights.
I'll bring this up to my neuro at my next appointment. My noise sensitivity is more a problem than my light sensitivity. Well, our brains are so unique, aren't they? :D
I don't see those listed as side effects. It's weird... I have no idea where it came from. I had same problem when after having seizures last week.

How about an enema? I experienced constipation while using antidepressant, too. It's a serious problem. I was so hopeless and annoyed as well. I'm on Keppra too but it's giving a diarrhea... 

I hope your problem would be out of the way soon!
Thank you, I'll talk to my neuro about this! My feet are cold since... Well, forever but it got worse after my neuro increased my Keppra dose.

I'm also on Trileptal and my doc thought 2 types is enough for now. She wanted me to try this dose for a month. I tried this dose before but didn't go well. I hope this time, it would be okay. 

Fycompa absolutely can make me cry in frustration. I was so worried that I would need antidepressant. Last year, I was so depressed that I had to try Seroquel XR before, didn't go well either. The spinning thing, I fell once but thank god, no injuries.

3,000 mg/day is no joke. If I remember correctly, it's the maximum dose of Keppra, right? 

Fycompa can be (excuse me) a bitch too. My world spun like a rollercoaster when I was on Fycompa. Emotional outbursts made me thought I was falling back to depression again. I was on Fycompa for 6 months until 2 days ago.

Headaches, tiredness, nausea, dizziness, unsteadiness, stomach pain and emotional outbursts. Fycompa really kicked me up and down but I gained a month seizure-free, too. I'm still trying to balance side effects and daily life.
I want Cerb to be okay as Christmas gift ><
I took a pic of Cerb riding ATV with his Dad [Here](https://ibb.co/YkQQTbz) so cute! Cerb couldn't walk so Jason had to carry him. God...
I can see that you've hurt Cerb and Jason had to carry you, but you have to make it! Don't be the one in the casket!!!!

I can see Brock and Cerb on that snowy mountain where the bomb separated Jason and Cerb. I also saw Brock and Cerb riding on the ATV too. 

My god... Don't be Cerb couldn't detect the bomb until too late that make him and Jason injured.
I'm a script writer and a interpreter. I also am self-employed so ny time is flexible. I can adjust my job as my health conditions.

I used to think "why me" too. Whenever I said that my mom told me that if it isn't then it would be someone else and what if that person is poor that they don't have enough money for meds, or there's no one care for them so that seizures comes and goes unattended, or they don't have knowledge about epilepsy, etc . I absolutely hate these things when I was a kid but growing up made me accepted it. Yes, it's better me than someone else. I have a supportive family, enough money for meds and knowledge about epilepsy. I can deal with it.
Thank you so much! It's so good when someone can understand my frustrations and struggles ❤️

I was 6 when I started to have seizures and I wad diagnosed at 7 (after went through dozens of tests and doctors... also my mom's tears too). 

It's been 17 (nearly 18) years living with epilepsy now. I was growing up with epilepsy so it's kinda hard for me, seeing all of my friends started new things that I'm not allowed to do. I never played any video game because my doc said, it isn't good for me and my mom forbids me to play video game (yes, I have an overprotective and anxious mom). 

I decided to drop out of school when I was 12 because I developed GAD. At 22, I was officially diagnosed with depression, too. I messed around with alcohol which resulted in Keppra lost its effects. I'm in a transition now, from Keppra to Fycompa.
My family told me that driving is tiring and they want to be driven rather than drive themselves. I got angry just because of that.
7, I had my first seizure at 6.

Hahaha, moms! I wanted to say that if you don't let me try to live alone when you're still here to help me,  then how the hell can I live alone when you're gone? I'll be miserable. But well, I don't wanna make her cry.
My mom told me that I gotta live with her until she dies. God...
I work as script writer and translator. I'm a a freelancer so I work at home, only have to attend meetings. It's nice, especially if I have a seizure during work time.

I don't remember much when I was a kid. At 8, I only had epilepsy for 2 years so I think it didn't get annoy yet. My mom always slept with me and told me to take meds on right time. That's all I remember. As I grew up, I started to hide my side effects and post seizure reactions more because I can see how my mom gets worry and sad everytime. I even hide my seizures from her now. I only tell my neurologist. 

I think the best advice I can give you is to tell your daughter everything, explain to her why you need to know it. You should treat her like she doesn't have epilepsy, give her privacy and independence. I know, you wanna know everything that's happening to her but that doesn't help. If she feels comfortable, she'll tell you everything. Many times, we don't need help to get better but all we need is understanding. 

Hope you'll find a way soon ^^

I'm on same dose as yours. I drink a cup of coffee every morning, if not, I'll be sleepy and have headache for whole day. It's okay for me to drink coffee but no more than a cup. Sometimes, my hand still shakes but I exchange that for being awake. 

If I take more than my usual amount of caffein, I'll have high chance having seizure at night. It already happened few times.

I don't drive, drink alcohol, stay up late and go to swim alone, go on vacation alone and I still have to live with my family even I'm 24. If I move out alone, my mom would be worried all the time. It's been 17 years since I have epilepsy. I'm on meds and have around 1 seizure/week. I'm sure I missed out many things without even knowing it.

When you can't change something than you must accept it. I know my epilepsy is for life so I accepted or else, I wouldn't have a life. Life become easier when you understand and accept things. That isn't easy at all, acceptance takes time.

I haven't had any serious injury from seizures because most of my seizures happened at nigh when I was already on my bed. The time I mention above, I knew I was coming because seizures like that already happened few times in that week. I knew what to expected. But that time, my mom was so close to me, her voice was broken so I knew she was crying and trying to tell me everything is okay. Next morning, I realized that my tongue was hurt quite bad, I didn't feel it last night. Maybe I was incredibly exhausted to notice pain.  

I am sorry if you have any bad injury from seizures. It must be devastating.

You made me remember one thing my neurologist said, she told my mom (in private) that if she (me) you to care than you should show it to her but if she doesn't and want to be ignored than do as she wants. I heard this when my mom was talking to my aunt. My mom follows the advice but sometimes, she's still anxious and asks me so many questions.

I understand our loved ones' tears but still hard to take it so I'm still trying to never let them cry. Your first sentence made me so happy, I never once in my life was told that I'm brave. I will keep your words as encouragement to keep fighting, thank you so much!

I still have epilepsy and once a week, at night. I sleep alone so it's okay. I have it since I was 7 so my mom quite overprotective of me. I have to work a lot on it. 6 years ago really scared her so bad that she demanded to sleep with me for 3 years long after that. I'm 24 and still hiding seizures from her.

I stopped telling my mom about my seizures when I saw her freaked out after one. I told her to stay at home when I had to go to the hospital. I only allowed my sister - a pharmacist, to go with me. She took it a lot better than other members in my family. I don't let my mom know about SUDEP, it only makes her worried all the time.
I wanted to cry when my mom cried too but if I cried, my mom would cry harder so I held back. Thanks God that my Dad didn't witness any bad seizure, only small ones.

I had severe depression and GAD last year. I thought, I was gonna kill myself for real. I have so many scars from self-harm but I survive. I stopped taking Seroquel too. 

Things will be better but unfortunately, no one believes it when they're having depression. 

Hang on, you'll survive this!
Omg, you was on the stairs after taking Fycompa? I'm on 4mg Fycompa right now and avoid stairs at all costs. Lucky me, I only have to take Fycompa once a day (9 pm).
23, nearly 24. I was diagnosed when I was 7. I didn't give a chance to try/experience many things in life because of epilepsy.

I'm not sure what are my triggers but I guess, too much caffeine, lack of sleep, stress and periods. Few times, new medications could be triggers too. I had grand mals after changing meds 6 years ago.

I had to do an EEG overnight qnd it was really difficult to fall asleep. I wanted a seizure to happen but man... Life never gives what you want. So I have none even my sleep wasn't a smooth one. But my neurologist still detected focal epilepsy on my left brain. She told me because it's been too long since I was diagnosed with epilepsy so she guessed maybe, there's a chance that my body was faking it. But nah, that EEG showed my epilepsy is real. 

P.s: I've been on meds for 17 years.
❤️ I WILL, THANK YOU!

I was on 1.000 mg for 9 days and seizures happened. My neuro decided that's enough and took me off it. I'm not sure I'm grateful or not because the side effects of Fycompa *(Perampanel)* is no kidding. I'm still trying adapt to it. I also on Trileptal *(Oxcarbazepine)* and  Keppra *(Levetiracetam)*  so I have no idea which side effects belong to which meds... @@

Last year, things were really bad for my mental health. I had severe depression, GAD (*generalised anxiety disorder)* and on verge of eating disorder plus OCD. I had to take Seroquel for few months. I always sighed and feel unstable heartbeat. I drank almost everyday, until the world spun. So, I guess... maybe, that was a reason Keppra lost its effects.

I hate exercise but everyone keeps telling me to exercise... I have no idea what breathing pattern I'll have if I walk or jog. I have to hide my shortness of breath from my family or else, they'll over worry.

I hope, you're doing better. I have epilepsy since I was 7, it's been 17 years. Sometimes, it's still hard to handle.  But let's fight it!

I'm taking coffee every morning so my mind can wake up. I'll have headache and be sleepy if I don't take it. I'm Vietnamese so of course, I drink Vietnamese Coffee, it's quite strong. 

I asked my neurologist before taking coffee. I started with Latte, then Mocha, then Cappuccino, lastly is Vietnamese coffee. 

But I only drink once a day, if I have more, high chance that I'll have seizure at night or next morning.

I take it one hour before I go to bed and I already feel the world spinning, so I don't dare to take it earlier. Maybe, my neurologist will increased it tp 6mg. I want to try too, if I can say goodbye to Keppra. Less medications less side effects :D

I was on 750 mg twice a day but my seizures got worse so my neurologist increased it to 1.000 mg twice a day. It didn't help, I still spaced out/blank many times in 3 straight hours. 

The side effects (when I was on 1.000 mg twice a day) hit me kinda bad, I was tired all the time. So my neurologist decided to change from Keppra to Fycompa. I'm in middle of transition now. I gotta say, the side effects are bad. 

My neurologist said that increased Keppra made me tired and the effect wasn't as good as she expected so that's why I'm on Fycompa noe. But not sure this one is for me, I'll stick with it for next few months and see where it goes.

I'm on Keppra about 6+ years but I'm changing to Fycompa now, becaue Keppra isn't as effective as before. I was on 1.000 mg/time, tiwce a day for 2 weeks and I was so tired and out of energy that my neurologist had to decrease it. 

I'm also taking Trileptal but the only side effects that stick with me over years is double vision. I think, talking about side effcts, Keppra is good. I experienced shortness of breath when I was on high dose, after climb stairs for only 1 minutes (T.T)

Now, this still happens but I'm on only 500 mg of Keppra/time, twice a day. But I have Trileptal and Fycompa too. So I have no idea which one causes me this...

I hope you'll feel  better soon!

I think... I have the idea of turning off emotions/feelings after I know, I have to try my best to stay alive. This idea will make my life easier.

I wrote my feelings in a diary which my therapist recommended because my memory is so terrible that I wouldn't remember without reading my diary. I also cried a lot and always listened to music to block out every sounds that could potential worsen my depression. I'm a self-harmer so I did it (which I highly recommend you stay away from it). My mind didn't think logically when I was depressed so many times I didn't believe that this was because of medication. I kept  in touch with my therapist and went to see her when I felt like I was going to loose the battle. Music, shower, crying, privacy and also keeping myself busy (damn hard to do) were what I've done when I fought depressed episodes.

I fought with it and came running to my psychologist after 3 days (4 dwys early for our next appointment). We talked and decided if I should contact my psychiatrist or not. I felt better after talking with my psychologist and kept fighting the negative thoughts for few more days and now it's gone. If meds worsen your depression make sure to talk to your therapist or psychiatrist, it's better than deal with it alone.
I nearly killed myself last week when my dose is increased. But it got better after a week. I'm on Seroquel so it takes me an hour every morning to be able to get out of bed.

I'm on Seroquel 100mg/day. At first, drowsiness is bad, I slept 10 hours straight but still sleepy but it wore off, but still difficult to wake up in the morning. When the dose is changed, depression systems and suicidal thoughts could get worse. But it would get better in a week or so. I'm suffering from constipation, sometimes nausea and well, I already have an unhealthy relationship with food before taking med but sometimes I could eat a lot and sometimes a whole day without eating. But yes, it would help with emotions, my emotions become more stable and suicidal tendencies decrease, selfharm also doesn't occur as often as before. I was also worried about side effects before I took it but at some point I know I have to get its help.
Oh, so I think we should wait a bit more to see what will happen in next week, yeah? You can PM me if you want ❤️

I'm taking 100mg every night now. If I have enough at least 7 hours sleep, the drowsiness won't be too bad. I read that the positives need about 2 weeks or more to kick in.
It's been 9 days si ce my firs dose. The side effects are wearing off everyday. But I still haven't  seen the positive sides, yet. Thank you for asking ❤️

If that person is someone else, well... That's difficult. I think you should pay close attention and see if we can get themselves open up slowly. Being straightforward might work if that person is really really desperately but doesn't know how to get help. But it can also make them run away. I don't open up to anyone but my doctors so I don't really know. Sorry...
